summary: FULL_POST_RELEASE_ACCEPTANCE=BLOCKED. Public provenance and the fresh Windows global lifecycle passed, but the required public upgrade path is broken: a public @ran-sh/dsh-crew@0.3.3 global launcher with an installed 0.3.3 managed payload runs `dsh-crew update`, reports `already current (0.3.3)`, exits 0, and leaves the payload at 0.3.3 even though public dist-tags.latest is 0.3.4. Refreshing only the global launcher to 0.3.4 then reports launcher 0.3.4 / payload 0.3.3 and recommends refreshing the launcher back to 0.3.3, so the required 0.3.3 -> managed payload 0.3.4 -> launcher convergence flow cannot complete. Per the TEST_ONLY contract, execution stopped at this released-product defect with no product fix. The real machine also began and ended with DSH Crew not installed, so installed-machine integration health and the real multi-role workload were unavailable. All task-created disposable homes, prefixes, caches, clones, payloads, and processes were removed; no publication, tag, Release, credential, official DSH, or product-source mutation occurred. final_machine_state: NOT_INSTALLED (unchanged from startup).

tests.name: T01 Startup revision, clean checkout, and Task Contract
tests.evidence: On main, git pull --ff-only origin main reported Already up to date; source_commit=LATEST resolved to c744370535899d91fa17289dc043331bf938e18e; git status was clean; task validator exited 0 with VALID TASK CONTRACT.

tests.name: T02 Public package, Git tag, GitHub Release, and immutable provenance
tests.evidence: Read-only npm queries returned @ran-sh/dsh-crew@0.3.4 and dist-tags.latest=0.3.4. Public npm pack returned exactly 88 files, shasum 318eaff92b488189cd868619f27729443e68323d, integrity sha512-nnjEjfX8DOF+IsDKk4SOIuAPub7qRek9j7dJuVQ90HeXMyEH8GPqlXSyRFvFfeGbs06oHjYkbkPx0/rydZesBQ==, and computed tarball SHA256 B40294103DB26883B3FAF8286E26FD4646DB65825DA6619FB7601CDAB5A2C80F. A disposable core.autocrlf=false checkout of d5a4fac00bcd90767e7d6d4ca0a23d48877e2b05 produced zero SHA256 mismatches across all 88 packed files. Annotated v0.3.4 peeled to that exact target and GitHub Release v0.3.4 exists (non-draft, non-prerelease). Historical peeled targets remained v0.3.0=e20f392a8babdaa4d37ffe3239ab3f8885a4a369, v0.3.1=dd414a352065e983e1be1b845287e99a50ade9c5, v0.3.2=17d3eb50ef74993e4ed61dba82a1bfef6659dd21; v0.3.3 had no Git tag and its GitHub Release lookup remained HTTP 404.

tests.name: T03 Fresh public Windows global lifecycle
tests.evidence: Under fully disposable HOME/USERPROFILE/APPDATA/LOCALAPPDATA/TEMP/npm cache/global prefix, npm install -g @ran-sh/dsh-crew@0.3.4 installed 190 packages and generated callable dsh-crew.cmd. install/status passed with payload 0.3.4 plus Harness/Codex/Claude installed. A full file-content hash snapshot before/after status was identical. After clearing transient npm cache inputs, status still passed. Reinstall and install were idempotent (one release directory before/after); live-registry same-version update passed and retained one release. Default uninstall kept the Crew config root; subsequent --purge removed it, all inside the disposable home.

tests.name: T04 Public 0.3.3 to 0.3.4 upgrade and convergence
tests.evidence: Minimal reproduction on Windows in a separate disposable HOME/prefix/cache: (1) npm install -g @ran-sh/dsh-crew@0.3.3; (2) dsh-crew install -> payload 0.3.3 and integrations installed; (3) dsh-crew update while npm latest=0.3.4 -> output `already current (0.3.3); repairing registration/integrations idempotently`, exit 0; (4) dsh-crew status -> launcher/candidate 0.3.3 and installed payload 0.3.3; (5) npm install -g @ran-sh/dsh-crew@0.3.4; (6) dsh-crew status -> launcher/candidate 0.3.4 but installed payload 0.3.3, with refresh instruction `npm install -g @ran-sh/dsh-crew@0.3.3`. The old launcher never resolves live latest and therefore cannot perform the required managed-payload upgrade.

The task required preserving the real machine's installed state, so this executor did not create a persistent installation merely to satisfy the check.

tests.evidence: Not run because the real installed-machine product/integration prerequisite was absent and execution had already stopped at T04. No provider credentials or official DSH stores were inspected.

tests.evidence: All task-created disposable homes, prefixes, caches, clones, payloads, and processes under the dedicated temporary root were removed; no task worktree was created; git status was clean before writing this Result Contract. No npm publication/dist-tag mutation, Git tag/Release mutation, credential access, official ~/.dsh access, package-manager policy configuration change, or product/source change occurred. Real machine state remained NOT_INSTALLED from startup to completion, which does not meet the required final_machine_state: INSTALLED acceptance criterion.

blockers: Released public-upgrade defect: @ran-sh/dsh-crew@0.3.3 `dsh-crew update` does not resolve npm latest=0.3.4 and leaves the managed payload at 0.3.3 while exiting 0; refreshing the launcher alone yields 0.3.4/0.3.3 divergence instead of convergence.

Environment prerequisite absent: normal product status reported the real machine's DSH Crew, Codex, and Claude integrations not installed at both startup and completion, so required installed-machine health and real provider-backed multi-role execution could not run without changing persistent machine state.
notes: This was TEST_ONLY. No package, source, test, implementation documentation, workflow, release, tag, registry, credential, or official DSH state was modified.

The first disposable lifecycle command encountered a PowerShell read-only variable-name collision before product installation; it was interrupted, normal product status was checked, and its task-owned temporary files were removed. The successful lifecycle rerun used unambiguous isolated variable names.
An npm cache-clean operation was scoped to the disposable cache only and did not change npm configuration or package-manager security policy.
The pre-existing unrelated git worktrees reported by git worktree list were not created, entered, modified, or removed by this task.
